What batteries do I need for my hearing aid? Finding the batteries you need for your hearing aid is easy, as there are standardized numbers and colors for each. If you’re not sure which battery you need, call us. Codes are 675 (blue), 13 (orange), 312 (brown) and 10 (yellow).

Frequently Asked QuestionsAbout Hearing Loss, Hearing Aids, & More

Below are the questions patients ask us most, answered plainly. If yours is not here, call the office and ask. We would rather answer it on the phone than have you guess. Audiology Associates of Westchester sees patients at our Harrison and Somers, NY offices, and from across Westchester County and Greenwich, CT.
What are the signs of hearing loss?

Speech sounds muffled. You follow words less well in a crowd or against background noise. Consonants go missing, so you hear that someone is talking but not what they said. You ask people to slow down or repeat themselves. The television goes up past what everyone else wants. You start withdrawing from conversations and skipping the places where conversation is hard. Hearing loss usually arrives slowly, which is why the people around you often notice before you do.
Is it hearing loss, or is it just earwax?

Both are common and they feel similar from the inside. A blocked canal makes sound quiet and the ear feel full, and it clears once the wax is out. Inner-ear loss makes sound unclear rather than quiet, and it does not clear on its own. An ear examination and a hearing test tell the two apart in one appointment, which is why we look in the ear before we test.
What happens at a hearing test?

The audiologist asks about what you are noticing and where, then looks inside both ears. Audiometric testing measures the softest tones you can hear across the pitch range. Speech testing measures how well you understand words. Tympanometry checks the eardrum and middle ear by changing the pressure in the canal, and otoacoustic emission testing gives a picture of the health of the hair cells. Afterwards we go through the audiogram with you and explain what it means before anyone talks about devices.
Who treats hearing loss?

An audiologist holds a master's or doctoral degree in audiology and can test for and treat hearing loss. A hearing instrument specialist supplies and fits hearing aids. An otolaryngologist, usually called an ENT, is a physician who diagnoses conditions of the ear, nose, throat, head, and neck. If what you have is a medical ear problem rather than a hearing problem, we refer you to an ENT.
How does a hearing aid work?

A microphone picks up sound and converts it to an electrical signal. The processor shapes that signal to match your hearing loss, and a small speaker delivers it into the ear canal. A hearing aid does not repair the ear. It makes the sound your ear still has more usable.
Will a hearing aid make my hearing normal again?

No. Damage to the hair cells of the inner ear does not reverse, and no device undoes it. What a well-fit hearing aid does is give the brain access to speech sounds it has been missing, particularly the high consonants such as s, f, th, and sh. Expect conversation to get clearer. Do not expect new ears, and do not expect a loud restaurant to be solved on the first day.
Why do I need two hearing aids?

You have two ears, and the brain compares what arrives at each one to work out where a sound came from. Wearing a single aid takes that comparison away, which makes locating sound harder and makes a noisy room harder still. Where both ears have loss, we fit both.
What styles of hearing aids are there?

Broadly, devices that sit behind the ear with a receiver or tube running into the canal, and devices built to sit inside the ear. Phonak Lyric is the outlier: it sits deep in the ear canal and stays in for months at a time. Which style suits you depends on your hearing loss, the shape of your ear, how your hands work, and what you need the device to do.
How long does it take to get used to hearing aids?

Usually a few weeks to a few months, and longer the more hearing you have lost. Wear them as much as you can rather than saving them for the hard situations. Keep a note of the moments you did not hear well and bring it to the follow-up, because those moments are what the adjustments are made from.
Can I try hearing aids before I buy them?

Yes. Every hearing aid we fit comes with a trial period. You take the devices home and wear them in your own life before you commit, and we go through the length of the trial and the return terms in writing first. The follow-up visits inside the trial are covered by the fitting fee.
Which brands do you fit?

Every major manufacturer, including Oticon, Phonak, Signia, ReSound, Widex, and Starkey. Fitting all of them means what we recommend is not limited by what we happen to stock. If a different brand suits your hearing and your hands better, that is the one we fit.
What is real-ear measurement, and why does it matter?

It is a probe microphone placed in your ear canal while the hearing aids are running, so we can see what the device is actually delivering at your eardrum instead of what the fitting software predicts. Ear canals differ, and manufacturer first-fit settings routinely fall short of prescriptive targets. A verified mid-tier hearing aid beats an unverified premium one. We measure at every fitting.
Can I buy hearing aids online instead?

You can, and they will arrive unprogrammed. Most of the work in a hearing aid is in the fitting: matching the output to your hearing loss, verifying it in your ear, and adjusting it once you have lived with it. A device bought online has had none of that done for your ears.
Does insurance cover hearing aids?

Coverage varies by plan, and the only reliable answer comes from your own insurer, so call them first. Medicaid sometimes covers the diagnosis and treatment of hearing loss, and some children's coverage falls under SCHIP. If your plan does not help and you do not have Medicaid or Medicare, call us.
What do hearing aids cost?

The cost depends on the level of technology and the features you need, so we quote after the evaluation rather than before it. When you compare providers, ask each of them what the price includes: the fitting, the verification, the follow-up visits, the trial period, the warranty, and what a future repair costs.
How do I look after my hearing aids?

Keep them away from heat, moisture, and hair products, and follow the cleaning instructions you were given. Turn them off when they are not in use, and replace batteries as soon as they run down. Keep spare batteries somewhere children and pets cannot reach them. Bring the aids in for a clean and check rather than waiting for them to stop working.
My hearing aid whistles, or my ear feels sore. Is that normal?

No, and do not keep pushing the device in. Whistling, soreness, or an aid that works its way loose usually means the dome, the receiver length, the mold, or the wax filter needs attention. Book a fitting appointment. This is not something to live with.
What should I do about ringing in my ears?

Tinnitus is a symptom rather than a diagnosis. It can come from earwax, from hearing loss, from noise exposure, or from a medication, and the first job is to find out which. Several of our audiologists are Certificate Holders of Tinnitus Management, and NYHD I TinnitusCare has been seeing tinnitus patients at our Harrison office since February 2024. Tinnitus in one ear only, tinnitus that pulses with your heartbeat, or a sudden drop in hearing should be seen promptly.

Hearing aids change sound waves to electrical signals using a microphone. The sounds are sent to a speaker in your ears.
Hearing Aid Fitting

Everyone needs something different from a hearing aid, and Audiology Associates of Westchester fits to the person rather than to a catalogue. We can find and fit your hearing aid, and we can show you how to use it and change the batteries.
Why You Should Have Two Hearing Aids

Wearing one hearing aid will make it difficult to tell where sounds are coming from and can make it hard to hear in loud areas. We always recommend wearing a hearing aid in each ear for the best results.

Which Brands of Hearing Aids Are Best?
Widex Hearing Aids
Widex is a family-owned company that has been advancing the hearing aid industry since 1956. They specialize in tinnitus solutions and create high-quality hearing aids like their EVOKE™ line.
Starkey Hearing Aids

Starkey Hearing Technologies was established back in 1964. They design all kinds of hearing aids, including ones that are receiver in canal, completely in canal, behind the ear, in the canal, and in the ear. They create some of the most advanced products, including ones that are smartphone compatible and have activity tracking capabilities.
Phonak Hearing Aids

Phonak hearing aids offer new solutions to hearing loss problems. Their products are continually changed to meet hearing loss problems. Their products include Phonak Audéo™ Marvel, Phonak Bolero™ Marvel, Phonak Sky™ Marvel, and many others.
Lyric Hearing Aids

Lyric creates extended wear, nearly invisible hearing aids. In fact, they created the Phonak Lyric™, touted as the world’s only 100% invisible hearing aid. All of their products are designed to provide superb sound quality.
Unitron Hearing Aids
Unitron creates simple yet effective hearing aids that have won numerous Red Dot awards. Some of their products include Moxi Now, Stride M, Stride P, Moxi Fit, and Moxi Kiss.
Signia & Siemens Hearing Aids

Signia has provided over 120 countries with high-quality hearing aids that deliver crystal-clear results. Siemens, under the Signia name, has provided customized audiology solutions for more than 100 years.
Rexton Hearing Aids
Rexton offers hearing aids and accessories to improve your quality of life. Their focus is on accessibility and personalization to make sure everyone in need of a hearing aid finds what they need.
Oticon Hearing Aids

Oticon has led the way for many changes in the hearing aid industry, recently with their Oticon Opn S™ and Oticon Opn Play™. These products can be used by children and adults who wish to hear clearly while enjoying an active life.
Resound Hearing Aids

ReSound has been offering hearing loss solutions to people of all ages since 1943. According to ReSound, its technology has earned the CES Innovation Award, the Die Goldene Concha award, and the Golden Lobe Award.
Caption Call
CaptionCall makes a transcript of phone conversations so you can see what the other person is saying. This is a real-time solution for those with hearing loss who have trouble using a phone.
CapTel
CapTel is a phone that amplifies the noise you want while reducing the noise you don’t want. It also provides a caption and transcript of the conversation.

Common Misconceptions About Hearing Loss
Hearing loss is a common, often misunderstood condition.

Hearing loss is extremely common; more than 10% of people in the United States have some level of hearing loss. Yet hearing loss can be hard to identify, and those with trouble hearing may be hesitant to seek help. If you are experiencing hearing loss, you are not alone. We would like to address your preconceptions about hearing loss. Read below to see common misconceptions about hearing loss.
Misconception: It would be easy to tell if I had any hearing issues.

Truth: Losing your hearing can happen over time, so you might not know that you’re having a problem. That’s why hearing tests are so important; a hearing test can help us identify hearing loss, no matter how subtle it is.
Misconception: Hearing solutions are so complicated, I might as well deal with the problem by myself.
Truth: Hearing loss affects the people around you as much as it affects you. Getting tested and finding the right solution is a shorter process than most people expect.
Misconception: I can wait to get hearing solutions.
Truth: Hearing loss can actually get progressively worse, so the sooner you can get a hearing aid or other hearing solution, the better.
Misconception: A hearing aid won’t work for me.

Truth: Hearing aids are not a one-size-fits-all solution. Cheap hearing aids probably won’t work, but a customized one will serve you well. We offer hearing testing and customized adjustments to make sure your hearing aid is fitted just for you.
Misconception: Everyone will notice my hearing aid.
Truth: Hearing aids have come a long way. Modern hearing aids are barely noticeable!
Misconception: A hearing aid will make me appear old.
Truth: Think about how young you’ll look and feel when you can participate in all the conversations happening around you! Plus, hearing loss doesn’t just happen to older people.
Misconception: Hearing aids cost a lot, and I can save money with a single one.

Truth: Although the initial cost of hearing aids may seem high, this investment is worthwhile and will pay off! Effective hearing aids will enable you to live a happy and healthy life. Also, we recommend getting two hearing aids to hear in a balanced way.

Hearing Tips
Our Hearing Tips

Most noise damage happens quietly, over years, and none of it comes back. That makes hearing one of the few things where the prevention is worth more than the treatment. These are the things we end up saying in the office most often.
85 decibels is where the damage starts

Any sound at 85 decibels or above can damage hearing over time, and the louder it gets the less time it takes. NIOSH puts the working limit at 85 dBA for eight hours. Ordinary conversation and a hair dryer sit below the line. Gunshots run from 140 to 190 decibels, which is why hunters and law enforcement officers need protection built for gunfire rather than ordinary foam plugs. Jackhammers and fireworks belong on the same list.
Give your ears time off

Turn the television and the radio down. When you are stuck somewhere loud, step outside for a few minutes, because distance and time both count. Give your hearing about 18 hours to recover after a long stretch of noise. With headphones, aim for roughly 60 percent volume for about 60 minutes at a time, then take a break. That is a rule of thumb rather than a medical threshold, and it fails you on a subway or in a gym, where the noise around you pushes the volume up. You should still be able to notice someone speaking nearby without taking the headphones off.
Nothing goes into the ear canal

Cotton swabs push earwax against the eardrum and can block the canal completely, so use them on the outer ear only. Ear candling does nothing useful and can burn you. If your ears feel plugged, allergies are a common cause and treating them helps. Persistent blockage is worth an appointment rather than a home remedy, because we can look in the ear and see what is actually there. And if you are turning the television up further than you used to, or missing words in a busy room, book a hearing test instead of waiting until you are sure. How to Take Care of a Blocked Ear
How to Take Care of a Blocked Ear

We’ve all had the experience, the annoying feeling when your ear is clogged and no amount of swallowing and yawning can make it feel better. You’ve attempted opening your ear canal with your finger, popping your ear, and even chewing gum. Sooner or later, you might think about giving up and just hope your ear unclogs on its own. And honestly, you wouldn’t be incorrect to try waiting a little bit to see if the problem goes away on its own unless, of course, you have pain, discharge, or other symptoms of an infection.Your Eustachian tube, a small passageway that attaches your middle ear to the space behind your nose and regulates the air pressure level in your ears, can get clogged if it stays open or closed for longer than it should. You might notice a popping and crackling noise in your ears as this tube closes and opens when you swallow or yawn. Normal hormonal changes cause the ear to stay open and viruses or ear infections will cause the ear to remain closed. It could take your ears a little while to go back to normal but both problems will recede over time.Another cause of clogged ears is buildup of earwax. Ear treatment can eliminate this type of clog, depending on the seriousness, this can be at home or at the hearing specialist. When managing plugged ears, here are some guidelines:
You Can Try Putting Hydrogen Peroxide Drops in Your Ear

Hydrogen peroxide can be utilized to break up earwax blockages, but it must be put in your ear correctly. Mixing the peroxide with luke warm water and using a pipette to gradually put it in your ear is the specialist’s suggestion. After you tilt your ear upward and put the drops in, a few seconds should be sufficient to dissolve the wax clog. You could have to do this a few times a day for a couple of days, but ultimately, the clog should clear up.
Don’t Put Anything in Your Ear to Clean it

Seriously, this is worth repeating: it will only make the situation worse if you try to use a cotton swab to clean your ears. Cotton swabs can cause complete blockage by forcing the earwax against the eardrum. Even earplugs and hearing aids can, in fact, cause an earwax blockage. In order to lessen earwax buildup, you should only use cotton swabs on your outer ear.
Your Allergies Need to be Treated

Plugged ears are commonly made worse by allergies. Follow your doctor’s directions about dealing with your allergies and don’t forget to take your medication. Avoid any unnecessary allergens, especially during allergy season.
Be Leery of Home Remedies That Sound Strange

You should not put a lit candle in your ear which should go without saying. Ear candling is an old practice of inserting a hollow candle in your ear and lighting it which is very unscientific. Theoretically, earwax is drawn into the hollow space in the candle when the heat of the flame creates a vacuum. This technique will likely cause more damage and probably won’t do any good. If something doesn’t sound accurate, it most likely isn’t and it’s best to contact a specialist. Don’t chance damaging your hearing by just trying things.If you don’t find any other solution, you should give us a call. Irreversible hearing loss or a ruptured eardrum are the kinds of repercussions you could sustain from incorrect earwax removal.

The Effects of Hearing Loss

Untreated hearing loss is hard on the people around you as well as on you. Conversations get shorter. Family events stop being worth the effort, and so do some of the things you used to enjoy. Improving your hearing starts with a hearing test at Audiology Associates of Westchester, which tells us what kind of loss you have and what will actually help.
Types of Hearing Loss

Different types of hearing loss call for different solutions, and the first job of a hearing test is to tell them apart. Conductive Hearing Loss: sound is blocked on its way through the outer or middle ear, often by earwax, middle-ear fluid, or infection, and it is frequently treatable and sometimes fully reversible. Sensorineural Hearing Loss: the hair cells of the inner ear or the hearing nerve are damaged, which is the most common permanent type, and well-fit hearing aids are the usual answer. Mixed Hearing Loss: a conductive problem sitting on top of a sensorineural one, so the plan usually has two parts, one medical and one technological. Sudden Hearing Loss: a rapid drop in hearing, usually in one ear, is a medical urgency and should be seen promptly rather than waited out. Find out which one applies by calling the hearing doctors at Audiology Associates of Westchester. We serve patients in and around Scarsdale, White Plains, Harrison, Rye and Mt. Hearing Protection - Tips to Keep In Mind

Did you know? 48 million people in the U.S. have trouble hearing with one (or both) of their ears and approximately 15% have noise-induced hearing loss because of loud work or leisure environments. While hearing loss cannot always be prevented, hearing loss due to exposure to loud noises is completely avoidable.Loudness is measured decibels (dB), and over time, any sound that is 85 decibels or higher can cause hearing loss — or other hearing problems, such as tinnitus. The louder a sound is, and the longer you listen to it, the more it can damage your hearing. Here are some tips on how you can protect your ears and prevent hearing loss: Turn the volume down when you are watching television or listening to the radio.When you are surrounded by loud noises, walk away and take a break to reduce your exposure.Give your hearing about 18 hours to recover after exposure to lots of loud noise.Use hearing protection devices (such as earplugs and earmuffs) when you cannot avoid loud sounds.Have your hearing tested as soon as possible if you're worried you might be losing your hearing.

Turn the volume down when you are watching television or listening to the radio.
When you are surrounded by loud noises, walk away and take a break to reduce your exposure.
Give your hearing about 18 hours to recover after exposure to lots of loud noise.
Use hearing protection devices (such as earplugs and earmuffs) when you cannot avoid loud sounds.
Have your hearing tested as soon as possible if you're worried you might be losing your hearing.

Psoriasis Affects More Than Your Skin

The word psoriasis usually recalls recollections of people with skin trouble like the people on all those advertisements. Psoriasis affects your general health and not only your skin. Psoriasis is often misunderstood and minimized, due to a lack of knowledge of how psoriasis impacts sufferers as well as the serious conditions that can be related to this disorder. Even though plaques on the skin are its most obvious symptom, they’re indicative of what psoriasis can do throughout the body. Continuous Irritation that can increase the danger of metabolic problems and cardiovascular disease.Psoriasis is also linked to another concern according to a different recent study: Hearing loss. Published in The Journal of Rheumatology, this research considered connections between psoriatic arthritis, mental health, and hearing impairment. Psoriatic arthritis has an influence on the joints, and is a kind of psoriasis, causing inflammation, difficulty moving, and soreness. The tell-tale plaques might not be experienced by people who suffer from psoriatic arthritis.In the same way as with rheumatoid arthritis (and like psoriasis), psoriatic arthritis is an autoimmune disease, the sufferer’s body is basically attacking its own healthy cells. But psoriatic arthritis is different from rheumatoid arthritis in that it’s usually asymmetrical (so you could have it in one knee but not the other), and it doesn’t only impact joints but leads to painfully swollen toes and fingers while it targets sufferer’s nails and eyes.Based on the findings of this recent study, hearing could also be impacted by psoriatic arthritis. The researchers contrasted the self-reported hearing loss of people who have psoriatic arthritis, people who suffer from psoriasis but not psoriatic arthritis, and a big control group of people with neither problem. They discovered that the group with psoriatic arthritis was more likely to report hearing loss, and audiometric screening supported the self-reports. Even when controlling for other risk elements, psoriatic arthritis sufferers were significantly more prone to suffer from hearing loss than either (the control group or psoriasis sufferers).But that’s not to say there’s no link between psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and loss of hearing. A 2015 study found that people who have been diagnosed with psoriasis are at a significantly higher danger of getting sudden sensorineural hearing loss, otherwise known as sudden deafness. With sudden sensorineural hearing loss, people’s ability to hear decreases significantly in three days or less. It has many potential causes, but scientists theorize that people who have psoriasis are at higher risk as a result of the kind of quick inflammation that occurs during a flare-up of psoriasis symptoms. The hearing may be impaired if this happens around or in the cochlea. This type of hearing loss, in many instances, can be helped by treatments that alleviate psoriasis, but hearing aids are often recommended when other interventions don’t seem to be working.It’s worthwhile to keep track of your hearing if you have psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis. Schedule regular hearing tests along with your annual health-care checkups. The inflammation from these diseases can lead to injury of the inner ear, which can cause psoriasis and loss of balance. psoriatic arthritis and psoriasis are both also linked to depression and anxiety, both of which can be additionally aggravated by hearing loss. Loss of hearing is something you want to catch early because untreated loss of hearing can result in other health problems like dementia.Awareness is key, and working with your doctors and periodically having your hearing evaluated can help you keep in front of symptoms with timely intervention. You shouldn’t have to sacrifice your standard of living for psoriasis or for hearing loss, and having the right team by your side can make a huge difference.

Types of Hearing Aids

Audiology Associates of Westchester can help you find the best type of hearing aid for your needs, but we welcome you to explore information about types of hearing aids below. Unlike older hearing aids, modern day IC hearing aids are nearly invisible and won’t stand out. In the Ear (ITE) Hearing Aids In the ear hearing aids are designed to help those who have disabilities or challenges, and they are made to fit the shape and color of your ear. Receiver in the Ear (RIC) Hearing Aids Receiver in the ear hearing aids are ideal for active adults in a professional environment who want to hear in meetings, parties, and other groups of people. The plastic can be hidden under your hair and the wire that fits in the ear is nearly invisible. These can also be compatible with Bluetooth to connect to your phone, iPad, or car.

Digital or Analog Hearing Aids

Analog hearing aids are ideal for quieter sounds and do allow manual tuning. However, they are not as flexible or advanced as digital hearing aids. Digital ones have the ability to identify specific outside noise and amplify the sounds you want to hear in a noisy situation. They also offer feedback cancellation, hands-free features, wireless technology, and the ability to program them.

If you would like the ability to pair your hearing aids directly with your smartphone or TV, wireless hearing aids may be the solution you want. Audiology Associates of Westchester can help you find wireless hearing aids and program them to suit you.

Why Choose the Hearing Doctors at Audiology Associates of Westchester?
Reason #1:Every hearing aid fitting is verified in your ear.

We put a probe microphone in your ear canal while the hearing aids are running, so we can see what the device is actually delivering at your eardrum instead of what the fitting software predicts. Ear canals differ, and manufacturer first-fit settings routinely fall short of prescriptive targets. We measure at every fitting, not only when it is convenient. That is what the Dr. Cliff Approved Provider listing is for.
Reason #2:You will see your own audiogram and hear what it means.

After the test we put the audiogram in front of you and explain what those lines mean for the rooms you are actually in: the restaurant, the meeting, the car. You should leave knowing what your hearing does and does not do before anyone talks about devices.
Reason #3:Doctors of audiology, and we refer out when the problem is not ours.

Our audiologists hold doctorates in audiology and New York State licensure, and several are Certificate Holders of Tinnitus Management through the American Board of Audiology. When what you have is an ear, nose, and throat problem rather than a hearing problem, we say so and refer you to an ENT. Cochlear implant candidacy testing, activation, and programming are done here rather than sent elsewhere.
Reason #4:The first appointment is a full diagnostic evaluation.

A case history, a look inside both ears, pure-tone testing across the pitch range, speech understanding, and middle-ear measures. How loud a sound has to be before you hear it and how clearly you understand words are two different measurements, and the second one is usually what brought you in.
Reason #5:Every hearing aid comes with a trial period.

You take the devices home and wear them in your own life before you commit. We go through the length of the trial and the return terms in writing first, and the follow-up visits inside it are already covered by the fitting fee.
Reason #6:We utilize the best brands.
We fit every major manufacturer, so what we recommend is not constrained by what we happen to stock. If a different brand suits your hearing and your hands better, that is the one we fit.
Reason #7:The follow-up is where hearing aids get good.

New hearing aids take a few weeks to a few months to settle, and the settings almost always need changing once you have worn them in your own life. Keep a note of the moments you did not hear well and bring it to the next visit. That list is more use to us than a general report that things are fine.
Reason #8:Clean-and-check between visits, and repairs when they are needed.

Hearing aids need cleaning, new wax filters, and small adjustments as the months go by, and we offer a clean and check service to keep yours working. If a device needs repair we handle that too. If you are pushing an aid in repeatedly, hearing it whistle, or feeling soreness, that is a fitting problem rather than something to live with.
